hints.content: The percentage of the Moon which is visible from Earth varies as a function of time. The figure shows the graph of this function. We can complete the description by *reading off the values* from the graph.

A *new moon* corresponds to $\blue{M=0\%}$ visibility. We see that this occurs when $\red{t=24}$ and when $\red{t=51}$. 
The first new moon was on the $24^{\textrm{th}}$ day of the year. The second new moon was on the $51^{\textrm{st}}$ day of the year.

To find the *period* between two new moons, we can calculate the difference between the first two times when the new moon occurred. 

$\qquad$ period $=51-24=\purple{27}$ days
Note that the word *period* can be used to describe any graph that shows a repeating pattern. The period is the length of the pattern that repeats**.**

The correct way to complete the sentences is as follows:

- The first new moon of the year was on day ${24}$.
- The second new moon of the year was on day $ {51}$.  
- Therefore, the period between two new moons is approximately  
${27}$ days long.

question.content:
The graph below describes the cycles of the Moon 
as observed from Earth during the first $60$ days of a year. 
The percentage of the Moon which we see varies as a function of time. 
A *full moon* corresponds to $100\%$ visibility
and a *new moon* corresponds to $0\%$ visibility. 

**Complete the following sentences based on the graph of the function.**


* The first new moon of the year was on day [[☃ input-number 1]].  
* The second new moon of the year was on day [[☃ input-number 2]].  
* Therefore, the period between two new moons is approximately  
[[☃ input-number 3]] days long.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: An XY coordinate plane a line plotted.  The horizontal x axis represents the time, in days, and runs from 0 to 60 in intervals of 3.  The vertical y axis represents the moon visibility, in percentages, and runs from 0 to 100 in intervals of 5. The line increases from (0, 15) until approximately (10.5, 100), then decreases until (24, 0), then increases until approximately (37.5, 100), then decreases until (51, 0), and then increases until (60, 70).  The line passes through the points (0, 15), (6, 80), (12, 95), (18, 40), (21, 10), (33, 75), (42, 75), (51, 0), and (54, 10).
